docs.title: Ordström system engineering reference
docs.text: This site documents the production dialogue runtime and the data languages used by the Handler, Pipeline, Tala, TDM, and DME. It is primarily an engineering reference; it does not imply that internal APIs or authoring formats are currently offered as customer-facing products.

docs.title: Historical material
docs.text: The archived Talkamatic documentation is retained for reference. Its tutorials and API descriptions are historical and should not be assumed to describe current production behavior.

docs.title: Runtime architecture
docs.text:
The current runtime has two HTTP boundaries that serve different callers:

  1. The Handler accepts application interaction requests.
  2. The Pipeline coordinates dialogue-processing services for the Handler.

Tala supplies DDD loading and shared semantic models. TDM's Dialogue Move Engine (DME) updates the dialogue state and selects moves from those models. NLU/NDU and NLG/NDG services participate in interpretation and realization; the Pipeline chooses and coordinates calls according to the request, session, configured endpoints, and enabled neural settings.

docs.title: Request path
docs.text:
Application
    │ interaction request
    ▼
Handler (/interact/{offer_id})
    │ prepares offer/session and forwards request
    ▼
Pipeline (/pipeline-fn)
    ├── language understanding and interpretation
    ├── DME dialogue processing
    ├── optional follow-up component calls
    └── response enrichment
    │
    ▼
Handler response to application

The Handler may load an offer when the session does not already contain its ODB. It forwards the request to the Pipeline, handles any service invocation requested by the Pipeline, and resubmits the result until a user-facing response is ready. It also applies Handler-specific behavior such as session encryption, wakeword handling, and response timing.

The Pipeline's request runner prepares session data, coordinates interpretation and DME processing, may restart interpretation after an ASR/NDU correction, then enriches the response and trims dialogue history. This is asynchronous service orchestration, not a single direct DME call.

docs.title: Repository ownership
docs.text:
Component Responsibility Main boundary/model Handler Application interaction boundary Session lifecycle and /interact/{offer_id} Pipeline Runtime orchestration Component calls and /pipeline-fn Tala DDD loading and semantic models DDD formats and shared model vocabulary TDM/DME Dialogue move processing Dialogue state and move selection

The production endpoint configuration is supplied to the deployed services. This site documents configuration names and behavior, not environment-specific URLs, credentials, or deployment values.

docs.title: Compatibility boundary
docs.text: The Handler contains compatibility behavior in addition to its main /interact/{offer_id} route. Treat those paths as compatibility behavior, not as the recommended application contract. Check the deployed Handler revision before relying on a detail described here.

docs.title: Handler interaction API
docs.text: The Handler is the application-facing runtime boundary. Its Azure Function route is interact/{offer_id}; it also contains a legacy interact route for compatibility. The production client contract uses the TDM interaction request envelope.

docs.title: Request envelope
docs.text:
The request is JSON with a version, session, and request operation. For example, a session-start request has this shape:

{
  "version": "3.4",
  "session": {},
  "request": {
    "start_session": {}
  }
}

Natural-language input is represented under request.natural_language_input; semantic input is represented under request.semantic_input. The request operation and the session are distinct: requests carry the current user event, while the client returns session state received from the preceding response. The Handler protocol also defines passivity as a request operation.

The offer_id in the route identifies the offer for the interaction. On session start, the Handler associates that offer with the session if no offer ID is already present. Continue a session by returning its response session with the next request.

The optional non_neural query parameter is passed as a request modifier. If the session does not already specify neural, a truthy parameter value sets session.neural to false; otherwise the Handler defaults it to true. Do not send the string false expecting it to be interpreted as Boolean false.

docs.title: Response and turn-taking
docs.text:
The response carries output, session, and, where relevant, context. output.moves describes the dialogue moves; output.utterance carries realized text when present. output.expected_passivity tells the client when to send a passivity request. The Handler may adjust passivity and speech completion timing, so client behavior should follow the response fields rather than hard-code a timeout.

The Handler adds a request ID when one is absent and propagates it through the request/session. Preserve the returned session as an opaque state object; applications should not edit DME-owned session fields.

docs.title: Session privacy
docs.text: The Handler encrypts non-whitelisted session fields into session.encrypted_data when session encryption is configured. It decrypts those values on the next request and merges them back into the session. Plaintext values take precedence if the same key appears in both places. Clients must round-trip session.encrypted_data unchanged and must not log or expose the session contents.

docs.title: Pipeline hand-off and service calls
docs.text: The Handler forwards interaction requests to the Pipeline. The Pipeline can return a service-call request instead of a final output; the Handler invokes the requested HTTP service, attaches its result, and calls the Pipeline again. This loop continues until the Pipeline returns a user-facing response or an error.

docs.title: Compatibility note
docs.text: The Handler also contains wakeword paths, including requests synthesized from wakeword activation, and an older interact route. Confirm behavior against the deployed Handler version before making either part of a new client integration.

docs.title: Pipeline API and orchestration
docs.text: The Pipeline is the service-to-service HTTP boundary called by the Handler. Its Azure Function route is pipeline-fn. The request body uses the same versioned interaction envelope that the Handler receives; the Pipeline adds and propagates a request ID and prepares the session before processing.

docs.title: Processing sequence
docs.text:
At a high level, the current implementation:

  1. Prepares the session and neural settings.
  2. Starts interpretation and dialogue processing.
  3. May correct the leading speech hypothesis through ASR/NDU and restart interpretation if the correction changes the utterance.
  4. Ensures the final interpretation and dialogue are present in the response.
  5. Enriches the DME output and trims dialogue history.

Individual NLU, NDU, DME, NLG, NDG, and VOG calls are conditional. Their endpoints are configured through FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_* application settings; for example, FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_DM, FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_NLU, FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_NDU, FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_NDG, and FUNCTION_ENDPOINT_VOG. Optional paths include ASR-NDU, AB-NDU, Q&A NDG, and system NDG. See pipeline/endpoints.py in the Pipeline repository for the complete current endpoint list.

docs.title: Request and response responsibilities
docs.text:
The Pipeline consumes JSON and returns a JSON response. Its internal PipelineRequest and PipelineResponse wrappers normalize access to the request, session, response, and request ID; they are implementation details, not separate wire formats.

Some responses represent an outstanding service invocation and do not yet contain output. The Handler owns the HTTP service round-trip and resubmits the result to the Pipeline. Do not treat every Pipeline response as a completed turn.

docs.title: Errors and deployment boundary
docs.text:
The Azure Function entry point returns the Pipeline response JSON on success. Unhandled exceptions are logged and returned as an HTTP 500 error object.

This endpoint is an internal production interface called by the Handler. Its presence in the codebase does not make it a supported standalone customer API. Coordinate wire-format changes across the Handler and Pipeline and validate them with their request/response tests.

docs.title: Runtime data languages
docs.text:
This reference uses Tala 31.0.1 (Git tag 31.0.1) as the DDD language baseline. The XML schemas, JSON schemas, parser/compiler, and tests at that tag define the contract; older Talkamatic prose is retained only for historical context.

The runtime crosses several distinct representations. Keep the authoring language, semantic language, interaction envelope, and DME state separate when tracing a request.

Representation Purpose Implementation reference DDD XML Domain, ontology, and service-interface source Tala XSDs and XML loaders DDD JSON Definition source format for ontology, domain, and service interface Tala JSON schemas and parser Semantic expressions Compact syntax for propositions, questions, goals, and moves Tala model/parser Interaction JSON Handler/Pipeline request and response envelope Handler/Pipeline contract TIS JSON / JSON:API DME information-state persistence and transfer TDM information-state serializers ODB Runtime offer data used to load DDDs and dialogue settings TDM backend and Handler offer loading

The formats are related, but not interchangeable. For instance, DDD XML is not the same thing as a semantic expression, and the serialized TIS is not an authoring DDD. Follow the links for the distinctions and source locations.

docs.title: DDD JSON
docs.text: DDD JSON is Tala 31.0.1's preferred definition source format. It supports a bundle or separate component files. Component objects use explicit names and arrays rather than XML attribute bags.

docs.title: Bundle and component roots
docs.text:
A bundle can be unwrapped or wrapped by a ddd key:

{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "ontology": {
    "name": "RoomBookingOntology",
    "sorts": [{"name": "room_type"}],
    "predicates": [{"name": "room_date", "sort": "datetime"}],
    "individuals": [],
    "actions": ["book_room"]
  },
  "domain": {
    "name": "RoomBookingDomain",
    "plans": [{
      "goal": {"perform": {"action": "book_room"}},
      "content": [
        {"findout": {"question": {"wh": {"predicate": "room_date"}}}},
        {"invoke_service_action": {"name": "BookRoom"}}
      ],
      "downdate_conditions": [{
        "in_beliefs_or_commitments": {
          "service_action_terminated": {"name": "BookRoom"}
        }
      }]
    }]
  },
  "service_interface": {
    "actions": [{
      "name": "BookRoom",
      "target": {"http": {"endpoint": "https://service.example/book-room"}},
      "parameters": [{"predicate": "room_date"}],
      "failure_reasons": ["unavailable"]
    }],
    "queries": [],
    "validators": []
  }
}

Each component may be stored separately with a root key: ontology, domain, or service_interface. Tala's ddd.config.json selects a bundle via ddd_bundle, or component files via ddd_files; ddd_bundle takes precedence when both settings are present.

docs.title: Domain JSON concepts
docs.text:
The domain object contains ordered plans. A plan has a goal and ordered content array, and may have postplan where allowed. Goals use {"perform": {"action": "..."}} or {"resolve": {"question": ...}}. Questions use tagged objects such as wh, yn, kpq, or alt. A condition and each plan item use a single-key object, for example {"not": {...}} or {"findout": {...}}.

downdate_conditions is the JSON spelling for explicit plan downdating. The downdate_plan field remains in the JSON schema for compatibility but does not create implicit DME downdating in Tala/TDM 31.0.1.

docs.title: Validation and loading
docs.text:
The Draft 2020-12 DDD JSON schemas are under tala/ddd/schemas/json/. Tests check the schemas against real fixtures and test bundle wrappers. DDDJSONCompiler converts DDD JSON to XML and passes it through the XML compiler; schema validity alone is not a substitute for compiler/loader tests.

The compiler also retains an XML-shaped structural JSON form using keys such as @, attrs, children, and items. Prefer the named component format for new DDDs; use structural JSON only when maintaining data that already depends on that compatibility form.

# From the Tala repository root, at the 31.0.1 source checkout:
source ~/python_3_11_environment/bin/activate
pytest tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_json_schemas.py
pytest tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_json_compiler.py

Keep DDD JSON distinct from JSON:API serialization of compiled DDD model objects. JSON:API has data/included resources and is used for runtime model interchange, not as DDD definition syntax.

docs.title: DDD source formats
docs.text: Dialogue Domain Descriptions (DDDs) provide the ontology and domain rules consumed by TDM/DME, together with service-operation declarations used by plans. This reference is based on Tala 31.0.1 (tag 31.0.1). The XML/JSON schemas, compiler, model code, and tests in that tag are the source of truth.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Component XML source Purpose Reference Domain domain.xml Goals, plans, conditions, questions, queries, and DDD dependencies Domain XML Ontology ontology.xml Sorts, predicates, individuals, and actions Ontology XML Service interface service_interface.xml Service actions, queries, validators, parameters, and targets Service Interface XML

The XML components have separate roots and schemas. Tala 31.0.1 includes XSDs for domain.xml, ontology.xml, and service_interface.xml in tala/ddd/schemas/.

docs.title: XML loading
docs.text:
Tala validates and compiles the XML DDD components into model objects. Domain logic names ontology concepts, and service plan items name operations declared by the service interface. Therefore, editing one component often requires checking its references in the other components as well.

An XSD-valid document is only structurally valid. The XML compiler applies additional semantic checks; an XSD-valid document alone does not establish that a bundle loads or behaves as intended.

docs.title: DDD JSON
docs.text:
Tala 31.0.1 also supports a JSON definition format. It uses the same component roots—domain, ontology, and service_interface—and may be stored as a bundle or in separate files. Tala's JSON compiler translates these components into the XML compiler path. See DDD JSON for structure, schema status, and examples.

DDD JSON is definition syntax. The JSON:API model representation used for compiled/runtime interchange is a different, internal serialization format.

docs.title: Domain declarations
docs.text: This page covers Tala 31.0.1 declarations outside the individual plan-item pages: goals/plans, question parameters, queries, iterators, validators, Other plan items.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
A goal declares either an action the system can perform or a question it can resolve. Tala's XML compiler requires type even though the XSD does not mark it required. A perform goal needs an ontology action; a resolve goal describes a question.

<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <plan>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="room_date"/>
    <invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/>
  </plan>
</goal>
Attribute Type Behavior type perform or resolve Required by Tala's XML compiler. action string Ontology action for a perform goal. question_type question type Resolve-goal question type; defaults to wh_question. predicate string Predicate for predicate-based questions. accommodate_without_feedback Boolean Suppresses the usual accommodation feedback. reraise_on_resume Boolean Controls whether feedback is produced when a goal resumes. restart_on_completion Boolean Restarts the goal when it completes. max_answers integer Maximum number of answers returned for a user question. alternatives_predicate string Predicate used to distinguish answers when several alternatives are allowed.

A goal can have one plan, a postplan, zero or more downdate_condition elements, and preferred, proposition, superaction, and legacy postcond children. Current completion behavior should use explicit downdate conditions. Postplans are for bookkeeping after a resolve goal is resolved or downdated; author them on resolve goals.

For a resolve goal with question_type="yn_question", include a proposition child to define the yes/no question. <preferred/> marks a goal as preferred unconditionally; a preferred proposition makes it preferred when that fact is present. Each superaction names an ontology action that groups the goal's action under a broader action. The schema retains postcond as a compatibility element, but the current compiler does not process it; use downdate_condition instead.

<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <preferred>
    <proposition predicate="travel_mode" value="business_class"/>
  </preferred>
  <superaction name="arrange_travel"/>
  <plan><invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/></plan>
</goal>
<goal type="resolve" question_type="yn_question">
  <proposition predicate="need_visa" value="true"/>
</goal>

docs.title: Plan and postplan
docs.text:
plan is an ordered sequence of plan items. The order defines the preferred dialogue path, while the DME may respond to user input using general dialogue capabilities. See the plan-item reference.

postplan is also ordered. It runs after a resolve goal completes and is intended for bookkeeping, such as forgetting temporary information or moving to a follow-up goal. A jump from a completed goal's postplan does not repeat the completed source plan.

docs.title: Question parameters
docs.text:
A parameters declaration keys on a predicate, optionally qualified by question_type. Its attributes in domain.xsd include:

Attribute Values / meaning question_type Question type; omitted for the default wh-question form. predicate Question predicate. source domain or service; incremental-search result source. incremental Enables incremental search. verbalize Controls whether the question is verbalized. allow_goal_accommodation Allows goal accommodation for the question. always_ground Controls grounding behavior. max_spoken_alts Maximum alternatives spoken; minimum 1. max_reported_hit_count Maximum hits reported; minimum 1. on_zero_hits_action Action run for zero hits. on_too_many_hits_action Action run when there are too many hits. sort_order Currently alphabetic.

The XML schema permits these children:

  • service_query — question used as the service query.
  • ask_feature — feature predicate to ask about; kpq="true" asks whether the user knows the embedded feature value.
  • alt — explicit proposition alternatives.
  • hint — contains one inform item, presented after negative acceptance.
  • proposition, resolve, perform — typed question/goal content.
  • related_information — related questions.
  • always_relevant — marks the question relevant across topic changes.

For incremental search with source="service", define service_query; the ask-features refine the search. background and graphical_type are not in the Tala 31.0.1 XML schema and should not be copied from historical examples.

docs.title: Domain query
docs.text:
A top-level <query> requires a predicate and one of three mutually exclusive query bodies:

  1. One or more <implication> elements. The antecedent may contain a single predicate proposition or a configuration of propositions; all propositions in a configuration must hold. Make the cases exhaustive for the expected state space.
  2. <select_at_random>, containing one or more individuals. A later call may return the same item again.
  3. <enumerate>, containing one or more individuals. Values are returned in declaration order; randomize="true" changes that order randomly.
<query predicate="greeting">
  <implication>
    <antecedent predicate="time_of_day" value="morning"/>
    <consequent predicate="greeting" value="good_morning"/>
  </implication>
  <implication>
    <antecedent predicate="time_of_day" value="evening"/>
    <consequent predicate="greeting" value="good_evening"/>
  </implication>
</query>

invoke_domain_query resolves a question through the matching domain query. An enumeration restarts after its final value; use has_more_items when the dialogue must distinguish the last item.

docs.title: Iterator
docs.text:
An <iterator> requires a name and one <enumerate> child. Its <enumerate> contains propositions and may specify randomize and limit.

<iterator name="room_iterator">
  <enumerate randomize="false" limit="5">
    <proposition predicate="room_type" value="single"/>
    <proposition predicate="room_type" value="double"/>
  </enumerate>
</iterator>

iterate assumes the next proposition. The has_more_items condition can branch once the iterator is exhausted.

docs.title: Domain validator
docs.text:
A domain-level validator describes accepted configurations of propositions. Its name identifies the validator; each configuration is a conjunction of propositions. This is different from a Service Interface validator, which is an external service operation.

<validator name="DestinationValidity">
  <configuration>
    <proposition predicate="destination" value="karlstad"/>
  </configuration>
  <configuration>
    <proposition predicate="destination" value="gothenburg"/>
  </configuration>
</validator>

The Tala XML compiler reads configuration children, and DDD JSON represents the same information in valid_configurations. The domain XSD's named validator type is less specific than the compiler's effective structure.

docs.title: Defaults and dependencies
docs.text:
Each top-level <default_question> declares a question that is considered by default in the domain. A <dependency> identifies a dependent question with its own type/predicate and one or more <question> children that it depends on. The relation marks those questions as connected for relevance handling.

<dependency type="wh_question" predicate="room_date">
  <question type="wh_question" predicate="room_type"/>
</dependency>

docs.title: Source formats
docs.text: Tala 31.0.1 defines the XML structure in tala/ddd/schemas/domain.xsd and compiles it in tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py. The corresponding DDD JSON properties are defined in tala/ddd/schemas/json/domain.schema.json; see DDD JSON for the source bundle form.

docs.title: Domain XML reference
docs.text: Baseline: Tala 31.0.1 (tala/ddd/schemas/domain.xsd, the XML compiler, and the DDD tests). A domain describes goals and their plans, plus the queries, question parameters, iterators, validators, default questions, and dependencies used by those plans.

docs.title: Root and top-level structure
docs.text:
domain is the document root. name is required; is_super_domain is an optional Boolean. The root can contain:

Element Purpose goal A perform-action or resolve-question goal and its plan metadata. parameters Question-specific response, search, and realization settings. query Domain answers by implication, random selection, or enumeration. iterator A named enumeration consumed by an iterate plan item. validator Valid parameter configurations. default_question A question considered by default. dependency A dependency between questions. 
<domain name="RoomBooking" is_super_domain="true">
  <goal type="perform" action="book_room">
    <plan>
      <findout type="wh_question" predicate="room_date"/>
      <invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/>
    </plan>
    <downdate_condition>
      <in_beliefs_or_commitments>
        <service_action_terminated name="BookRoom"/>
      </in_beliefs_or_commitments>
    </downdate_condition>
  </goal>
</domain>

The example assumes that book_room is an ontology action, room_date is an ontology predicate, and BookRoom is declared in the service interface.

docs.title: Goals and questions
docs.text:
The compiler requires goal/@type: perform or resolve. A perform goal names an ontology action. A resolve goal names a question. The schema's question types are goal, wh_question, kpq, alt_question, and yn_question; the question's predicate/proposition must be compatible with the ontology.

The schema permits goal children for plan, legacy postcond, explicit downdate_condition, postplan, proposition, preferred, and superaction. Use explicit downdate_condition elements for current plan-completion semantics; postcond is a deprecated form.

docs.title: Plans and plan items
docs.text:
Plan items are interpreted in document order. The Tala 31.0.1 XML schema recognizes:

forget, forget_shared, forget_all, log, greet, invoke_service_query, invoke_domain_query, findout, raise, bind, invoke_service_action, get_done, assume_issue, assume_shared, assume_system_belief, inform, if, once, jumpto, signal_action_completion, signal_action_failure, end_turn, reset_domain_query, iterate, and change_ddd.

if contains one condition and optional then/else plans. once contains plan items and supports an optional id. findout, raise, service/domain queries, and several other items refer to the question language above; their individual XML attributes are defined in domain.xsd and compiled by tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py.

docs.title: Conditions and downdating
docs.text:
Condition expressions include and, or, not, has_value, has_shared_value, has_private_value, in_shared_commitments, in_private_beliefs, in_beliefs_or_commitments, and has_more_items. and/or contain one or more child conditions; not contains exactly one.

The in_* forms accept either predicate/value attributes or one child proposition. Child forms include predicate propositions, perform/resolve goals, service-action started/terminated propositions, action/question status, resolvedness, and knowledge-precondition propositions. For example:

<in_beliefs_or_commitments>
  <service_action_terminated name="BookRoom"/>
</in_beliefs_or_commitments>

service_action_terminated means the service call has terminated; it does not indicate success. TDM stores the proposition in shared commitments or private beliefs depending on postconfirmation, which is why in_beliefs_or_commitments can be useful in a downdate condition.

Compatibility detail: domain.xsd declares invoke_service_action/@downdate_plan with an XSD default of true, but Tala 31.0.1's XML compiler defaults a missing attribute to false, and the DDD model no longer derives implicit downdate conditions from it. Do not use this attribute to end a plan; specify an explicit downdate_condition. Tala tests cover the no-implicit-downdate rule.

docs.title: Queries and question parameters
docs.text:
A domain query declares a predicate and one of three forms: one or more implications, select_at_random, or enumerate. An iterator wraps an enumeration and can set randomize and limit. has_more_items checks either a predicate-backed query or a named iterator.

Question parameters configure options including source, incremental, verbalize, always_ground, allow_goal_accommodation, hit limits, zero-hit/too-many-hit actions, service queries, alternatives, ask-features, hints, and always-relevant behavior. The complete field/child contract is in domain.xsd. <background> is not in the Tala 31.0.1 domain schema; do not use historical background examples as current syntax.

docs.title: Executable sources
docs.text:

  • XML compiler and semantic checks: tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py
  • Focused tests: tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py

docs.title: DME information state
docs.text: The Dialogue Move Engine maintains a TDM Information State (TIS) while processing a session. It contains shared dialogue state and private engine state; it is runtime state, not a DDD or an application-owned object.

docs.title: Main structure
docs.text:
The current TDM model has shared and private parts. Shared state includes previous moves, the latest utterance and turn content, questions under discussion (QUD), active goals, commitments, and a previous goal. Private state includes the agenda, beliefs, issues being accommodated, iterators, question hints, the next-move queue, the active plan, and temporary data.

The exact structure is defined by the DME Information State contract. Changes to state fields can affect persistence and session compatibility.

docs.title: Serialization and storage
docs.text:
TDM exposes JSON:API serialization for its state resources and also serializes the TIS as JSON for persistence. The CouchDB session retriever stores this serialized TIS with the TDM session record and returns a compressed serialized form to the caller. The Pipeline and Handler also carry session fields across interaction requests; that outer session envelope is distinct from the TIS serialization itself.

Use the versioned state contract when changing this format. Do not hand-edit persisted production session state based only on an example from the documentation.

docs.title: Important distinction
docs.text: The Handler response session is the application round-trip object. It can contain offer data, request metadata, dialogue history, and other fields in addition to DME state. The Handler can encrypt non-whitelisted session values under session.encrypted_data. Neither that wrapper nor the encrypted values should be confused with the TIS's own JSON/JSON:API representation.

docs.title: Ontology XML reference
docs.text: Baseline: Tala 31.0.1. An ontology gives domain plans and semantic interpretations their typed vocabulary: sorts, predicates, individuals, and actions.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
ontology is the document root and requires a name. It can contain any number of these declarations:

<ontology name="RoomBookingOntology">
  <sort name="room_type"/>
  <predicate name="room_date" sort="datetime"/>
  <predicate name="selected_room" sort="room_type" multiple_instances="false"/>
  <individual name="single" sort="room_type"/>
  <action name="book_room"/>
</ontology>
Declaration Required attributes Optional attributes sort name dynamic predicate name, sort feature_of, multiple_instances individual name, sort — action name —

Tala 31.0.1 has these built-in sort names: boolean, integer, datetime, real, string, image, domain, webview, and person_name. Declare application-specific sorts in the ontology before using them in predicates or individuals. XML Boolean attributes use lowercase true/false.

docs.title: Sorts and individuals
docs.text:
A sort is the ontology's value type. Custom sorts can be marked dynamic="true" when the running domain must introduce individuals not declared as static entries. Individuals pair a name with a sort; their values are subsequently checked and normalized according to that sort.

<sort name="room_type"/>
<sort name="album_name" dynamic="true"/>
<individual name="single" sort="room_type"/>

integer, real, boolean, datetime, and person_name have corresponding Tala value normalization. image, webview, and domain are also built-in sorts; inspect their semantic model when defining values for those types.

docs.title: Predicates and actions
docs.text:
A predicate names a property and the sort of its value. feature_of associates a predicate with a parent predicate, as used by question-feature behavior. multiple_instances="true" allows multiple values for the predicate in domains that need a set of alternatives.

<predicate name="selected_room" sort="room_type" multiple_instances="true"/>
<predicate name="room_capacity" sort="integer" feature_of="selected_room"/>
<action name="book_room"/>

Predicate names are used in proposition expressions and DDD question/condition elements. Action names are used by perform goals and service invocations. A service-interface operation name (for example BookRoom) is a separate name; declare the semantic action (book_room) and service operation independently.

docs.title: References and validation
docs.text:
Domain goals and propositions refer to ontology action and predicate names. Tala compiles the ontology first and uses it while compiling the domain, so unknown names or incompatible values can fail DDD loading even when XML is well-formed.

  • Structure: tala/ddd/schemas/ontology.xsd
  • DDD JSON schema: tala/ddd/schemas/json/ontology.schema.json
  • Compiler/model: tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py, tala/model/ontology.py, tala/model/sort.py, and tala/model/predicate.py

docs.title: Plan items
docs.text:
This page documents the remaining Tala 31.0.1 plan items. They are directives inside the ordered <plan>/<postplan> sequences or conditional branches described in Domain declarations. The XML language and plan-item set are defined by domain.xsd and the Tala compiler.

Detailed pages for Findout, Bind, Conditions, Downdate conditions, and Invoke service action are separate.

docs.title: raise
docs.text:
<raise type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>

raise raises a question/issue for the user but does not put the same answer-resolution requirement on the current plan as findout. type defaults to wh_question; the question may be goal, WH, KPQ, alternative, or yes/no. It accepts the same question-content children as findout. The allow_answer_from_pcom and alts_predicate options belong to findout, not raise.

docs.title: assume_issue
docs.text:
<assume_issue type="wh_question" predicate="departure_time"/>

This opens a question issue as if the user had asked it. The issue should have a matching resolve goal in the DDD. It supports question content such as a KPQ's embedded_question; insist is an optional Boolean. Tala 31.0.1's XML compiler requires type, even though the schema leaves it optional.

docs.title: assume_shared and assume_system_belief
docs.text:
Each contains a predicate proposition. assume_shared adds the fact to shared commitments; assume_system_belief adds it to private beliefs.

<assume_shared>
  <proposition predicate="current_recipe" value="sourdough_starter"/>
</assume_shared>
<assume_system_belief>
  <proposition predicate="quantity" value="200"/>
</assume_system_belief>

The proposition must use an ontology predicate and a value compatible with its sort. These are assertions of known state, not service calls or validators.

docs.title: inform
docs.text:
<inform insist="false" generate_end_turn="true" expected_passivity="2.0">
  <proposition predicate="first_name" value="Charlie"/>
</inform>

inform contains one predicate proposition. It makes the proposition shared and requests a system utterance. With the default insist="false", an existing shared value for that predicate suppresses the inform. With insist="true", the previous value for the predicate is forgotten before the new proposition is assumed and informed. generate_end_turn defaults to false; when true, the compiler also adds an end-turn with the specified expected_passivity (default 0.0 seconds).

docs.title: Forgetting state and requesting user actions
forget and forget_shared
docs.text:
Use a predicate attribute to forget every matching proposition or a proposition child to forget one value:

<forget predicate="colour"/>
<forget>
  <proposition predicate="transport" value="train"/>
</forget>
<forget_shared predicate="colour"/>

forget removes the target from private beliefs and shared commitments. forget_shared removes it from shared commitments while leaving private beliefs unchanged.

docs.title: forget_all
docs.text:
<forget_all/>

This is a broad dialog-state reset: active plan and goals, private beliefs, shared commitments, and previous utterance traces are cleared, then the top goal is restarted. It has no attributes or children; use it only when restarting the dialogue is intended.

docs.title: get_done
docs.text:
<get_done action="add_water" step="1"/>

action is a required ontology action; step is an optional integer. The system asks the user to carry out that action. The item completes when the user reports that the action is done. A get_done may contain alt children to represent alternative actions.

docs.title: if
docs.text:
<if>
  <has_shared_value predicate="sourdough_status"/>
  <then><jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/></then>
  <else><jumpto type="perform" action="start_sourdough"/></else>
</if>

if contains exactly one condition expression, followed by optional then and else plans. Either branch may itself contain plan items, including nested if items. A missing branch does nothing.

docs.title: once
docs.text:
<once id="initial_greeting">
  <inform>
    <proposition predicate="welcome_message" value="welcome"/>
  </inform>
</once>

once wraps a plan sequence and runs it once for its marker. With no id, Tala assigns a unique marker. Reusing an id shares the once-state across blocks. The marker is kept in private beliefs, so forgetting it makes the block eligible to run again.

docs.title: jumpto
docs.text:
<jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/>

jumpto accepts a goal descriptor. Tala's compiler requires type; for a perform-goal target, supply its ontology action. The target plan is loaded, then the original plan resumes from its beginning. An unguarded jump may be encountered repeatedly; guard it with if or once. A jump in a completed resolve goal's postplan does not have that loop behavior.

docs.title: change_ddd
docs.text:
<change_ddd name="navigation"/>

name selects another DDD for the session. A domain change replaces the current DDD-specific plan/goal context; it is not a jump to a goal within the same domain.

docs.title: invoke_service_query
docs.text:
<invoke_service_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"
                      min_results="1" max_results="2"/>

Invokes the service-interface query associated with the question. type defaults to wh_question; min_results and max_results default to 1. Raise max_results when multiple service results are expected. Question content may use the applicable proposition or embedded-question children.

docs.title: invoke_domain_query
docs.text:
<invoke_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"/>

Invokes the top-level domain query matching the question in the active DDD. The Tala compiler sets both result bounds to one for this plan item.

docs.title: iterate
docs.text:
<iterate iterator="nice_destinations"/>

iterator is required and names a top-level iterator. The item assumes the next proposition in its enumeration. Use <has_more_items iterator="nice_destinations"/> to test whether values remain.

docs.title: reset_domain_query
docs.text:
<reset_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="season_to_consider"/>

Resets enumeration state for the domain query identified by the question. The question uses the same type/child syntax as findout and domain queries.

docs.title: signal_action_completion
docs.text:
<signal_action_completion postconfirm="false"/>

Signals that the containing perform goal is complete, stopping the remainder of its plan. By default, TDM reports a successful action-status move; postconfirm="false" suppresses that report. An optional action targets a named ontology action instead of the containing goal.

docs.title: signal_action_failure
docs.text:
<signal_action_failure reason="service_unavailable"/>

reason is required. Without action, it aborts the containing perform goal and stops the rest of its plan. With action, it marks that action aborted and allows the containing plan to continue. The failure reason is a result label; it is not declared in the ontology.

docs.title: end_turn
docs.text:
<end_turn expected_passivity="1.5"/>

expected_passivity is a required decimal number of seconds. end_turn hands the turn to the client/user at that point even if the DME otherwise has more plan content. It controls this explicit handoff, not passivity timing globally.

docs.title: log
docs.text:
<log message="About to invoke BookRoom" level="debug"/>

message is required. level is optional and defaults to debug in Tala's compiler. The log entry is diagnostic, not a user-facing dialogue move.

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
<greet/>

An empty plan item that requests a greeting move.

docs.title: DDD JSON
docs.text:
Plan items use a single-key object in DDD JSON. For example:

{"forget": {"predicate": "colour"}}
{"if": {"condition": {"has_value": {"predicate": "destination"}}, "then": [{"greet": {}}]}}
{"once": {"id": "initial_greeting", "content": [{"greet": {}}]}}
{"signal_action_failure": {"reason": "service_unavailable"}}

The exact payload schemas are under tala/ddd/schemas/json/domain.schema.json.

docs.title: Semantic expressions, moves, and interpretations
docs.text: Baseline: Tala 31.0.1. Tala models dialogue semantics as typed objects and converts them to and from JSON. Semantic expressions are a compact textual notation for propositions, questions, goals, and moves in DDDs and interaction data. The parser is tala/ddd/parser.py; model encoders/decoders live in tala/model/.

docs.title: Interpretation JSON
docs.text:
Tala's Interpretation model reads an interpretation object with modality, moves, and, when required by the modality, utterance. A move is parsed into a typed user-move object. perception_confidence is optional. Supported modalities and whether they require utterance text are defined by Tala's Modality model.

An interaction request can supply interpretations as request.semantic_input.interpretations. Alternatively, speech input arrives as request.natural_language_input.hypotheses and the Pipeline adds interpretations during processing.

An interpretation's moves are structured move objects. A user move includes semantic_expression, perception_confidence, and understanding_confidence; a DDD-specific move also includes ddd. The interpretation includes modality, moves, and (for text/speech modalities) utterance. Tala 31.0.1 supports text, speech, haptic, and other; text and speech require utterance text.

docs.title: Core expression forms
docs.text:
These forms are exercised by Tala's parser tests:

Meaning Expression Predicate proposition dest_city(paris) Nullary proposition need_visa() Perform goal goal(perform(book_room)) Resolve goal goal(resolve(?X.dest_city(X))) User requests an action request(book_room) Ask a wh-question ask(?X.dest_city(X)) Answer with a predicate/value answer(dest_city(paris)) Positive grounding of a proposition icm:und*pos:USR*dest_city(paris) Service action has terminated service_action_terminated(BookRoom)

Question expressions use a typed variable form such as ?X.predicate(X) for a wh-question. The parser also supports yes/no, alternative, knowledge precondition, and nested goal questions. Proposition arguments are interpreted using the active DDD ontology, so names and values are not untyped free text.

docs.title: Semantic object families
docs.text:
The model layer represents propositions, questions, goals, actions, predicates, individuals, and sets, along with user/system moves. These are structured objects, not arbitrary strings. Their JSON representation is implemented by the relevant as_dict methods and the semantic-expression parser in Tala.

ICMs (interaction control moves) include perception (per), acceptance (acc), semantic grounding (sem), understanding (und), and structure control moves such as reraise, accommodate, resume, report_inference, and loadplan. Polarity and any semantic content are part of the move representation. For example, icm:acc*neg:issue is a negative acceptance of an issue. cardinal_sequencing carries an integer step. Use Tala's ICM.create(...) and parser/model tests to check valid type/content combinations.

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text: Use Tala's tala/model/ classes and parser tests as the serialization source of truth. This notation describes semantic objects; it does not define which understanding or realization service produces them. The archived formalism guide explains historical concepts but may not cover current model extensions.

docs.title: Service Interface XML reference
docs.text: Baseline: Tala 31.0.1. The service interface declares operations referenced by domain plan items and binds them to parameters and transport targets.

docs.title: Operations and required structure
docs.text:
The root <service_interface> contains action, query, and validator declarations. An action has this structure:

<service_interface>
  <action name="BookRoom">
    <parameters>
      <parameter predicate="room_date" format="value"/>
      <parameter predicate="selected_room" optional="true"/>
    </parameters>
    <failure_reasons>
      <failure_reason name="unavailable"/>
    </failure_reasons>
    <target>
      <http endpoint="https://service.example/book-room"/>
    </target>
  </action>
  <query name="FindRooms">
    <parameters>
      <parameter predicate="room_date"/>
    </parameters>
    <target>
      <http endpoint="https://service.example/find-rooms"/>
    </target>
  </query>
</service_interface>

The example endpoint is illustrative only; deployed endpoint values belong in service configuration.

Operation Required children Target forms accepted by Tala 31.0.1 action parameters, failure_reasons, target <frontend/> or <http endpoint="..."/> query parameters, target <http endpoint="..."/> validator parameters, target <http endpoint="..."/>

Operation names must be unique within their type. A target is required. Query and validator frontend targets are rejected by Tala's XML compiler tests.

For an action, keep the <parameters>, <failure_reasons>, and <target> children even when a section is empty. An empty failure list is written as <failure_reasons/>. Queries and validators do not have a failure_reasons child in the XML format.

docs.title: Parameters and results
docs.text:
Each <parameter> requires an ontology predicate. Its optional format is value or grammar_entry; optional is an XML Boolean. For HTTP targets the service receives both the semantic value and the language grammar entry. The format selector chooses the frontend representation for frontend-targeted actions.

Actions may declare failure_reason names. The action result and failure information are consumed by TDM's service-action execution and reporting logic.

Parameter attribute Values Meaning predicate Required ontology predicate Selects the argument to bind and pass to the target. optional XML Boolean Marks the argument optional. format value or grammar_entry Selects the frontend argument form. HTTP targets receive both representations.

frontend delegates actions to the application-facing side. http invokes the declared HTTP endpoint; query and validator operations use this target in Tala 31.0.1.

docs.title: Compatibility boundaries
docs.text:
The XSD declares an entity_recognizer element, but Tala 31.0.1's ServiceInterfaceCompiler builds only actions, queries, and validators. Do not assume an entity-recognizer declaration is part of the runtime ServiceInterface model.

The DDD JSON schema uses a shared target shape that permits a frontend target for all operation types. The XML compiler rejects frontend targets for queries and validators after JSON is converted to XML. Use HTTP targets for those operations and compile/load the bundle to validate it.

Executable references: tala/ddd/schemas/service_interface.xsd, tala/ddd/schemas/json/service_interface.schema.json, tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py, and tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py.

docs.title: Bind
docs.text: Tala 31.0.1 XML element: a plan item declaring a question that can be answered or accommodated from user input, but which the plan does not ask the user to answer. It is commonly used for optional parameters.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
<bind type="wh_question" predicate="price_class"/>

type and predicate describe the question using the same question model as findout. The default type is wh_question. A bind can contain the same question children supported by the shared question XML structure, including alt and embedded_question where appropriate.

bind can appear in a goal plan, postplan, or an if branch. Its question content can be supplied by type/predicate attributes or by the question children described in Findout: proposition, perform, resolve, alt, or embedded_question.

Attribute Type Default Meaning allow_binding_yn_answers Boolean false Allows relevant yes/no answers to bind to a yes/no question in the active plan.

The compiler rejects allow_binding_yn_answers="true" unless the bind question is yes/no. DDD JSON has the same Boolean option; compilation rejects the flag on a non-yes/no question there as well.

docs.title: Behavior and placement
docs.text:
A bind does not produce a question prompt. It lets TDM consider a relevant user answer for the bound question while the bind remains in the active plan. When the DME executes the bind plan item, it removes it from the plan. Place a bind after plan items that need it—usually at the end of the plan—or it can be removed before later steps can consume an answer.

The DME considers compatible user propositions for questions still present in the plan. Yes/no answers are excluded unless a matching yes/no bind explicitly sets allow_binding_yn_answers="true".

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Optional WH parameter:

<plan>
  <findout type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
  <bind type="wh_question" predicate="price_class"/>
</plan>

Yes/no bind:

<bind type="yn_question" predicate="need_visa"
      allow_binding_yn_answers="true"/>

DDD JSON:

{
  "bind": {
    "question": {"yn": {"predicate": "need_visa"}},
    "allow_binding_yn_answers": true
  }
}

See domain XML, DDD JSON, and the archived Bind examples.

docs.title: Tala reference and tests
docs.text:
• XML compiler validation: tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py
  • Model and JSON form: tala/model/plan_item.py, tala/ddd/json_parser.py
  • Tala tests: tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py and tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_json_compiler.py

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text: Conditions are expressions evaluated against the TDM Information State. In Tala 31.0.1 they appear in if plan items and inside a goal's downdate_condition.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
<has_value predicate="p"/>
<has_shared_value predicate="p"/>
<has_private_value predicate="p"/>
<in_shared_commitments predicate="p" value="x"/>
<in_private_beliefs predicate="p" value="x"/>
<in_beliefs_or_commitments predicate="p" value="x"/>
<has_more_items predicate="p"/>
<has_more_items iterator="i"/>
<and>
  <has_value predicate="p"/>
  <not><in_private_beliefs predicate="p" value="x"/></not>
</and>

Conditions can be nested inside other conditions. They do not have standalone effects: they select an if branch or determine whether a goal may be downdated.

docs.title: Condition forms
docs.text:
Form True when has_value The predicate occurs in shared commitments or private beliefs. has_shared_value The predicate occurs in shared commitments. has_private_value The predicate occurs in private beliefs. in_shared_commitments The specified proposition is in shared commitments. in_private_beliefs The specified proposition is in private beliefs. in_beliefs_or_commitments The specified proposition is in either store. has_more_items A domain query enumeration or named iterator has more items. and, or, not Boolean combinations of nested condition expressions.

The XML attributes are:

Attribute Applies to Meaning predicate has_*_value; attribute form of in_*; predicate-form has_more_items Ontology predicate whose fact/value is checked. value Attribute form of in_* Individual value. Omit it only for a nullary predicate. iterator Iterator-form has_more_items Iterator whose remaining values are checked.

has_value, has_shared_value, and has_private_value require a predicate attribute. For in_*, predicate is used with the optional value attribute or a child proposition instead.

has_*_value tests whether a predicate has any stored value; it does not test for one particular value. For in_*, the proposition may be supplied by predicate/value attributes or as a child proposition. Child forms supported by the Tala 31.0.1 compiler include predicate propositions, perform, resolve, service_action_started, service_action_terminated, action_status, question_status, resolved, and know_answer.

docs.title: Parents and children
docs.text:
• Parent expressions: if and downdate_condition.
  • and and or contain one or more condition expressions; not contains exactly one. in_* conditions contain at most one proposition child.

docs.title: Attribute and child forms
docs.text:
Attribute form for a predicate/value proposition:

<in_shared_commitments predicate="flight_status" value="late"/>

For a nullary predicate, omit value. For non-nullary predicates, provide a value of the ontology-declared sort.

Scope-specific value checks:

<has_value predicate="flight_status"/>
<has_shared_value predicate="flight_status"/>
<has_private_value predicate="flight_status"/>
<in_private_beliefs predicate="flight_status" value="late"/>
<in_beliefs_or_commitments predicate="flight_status" value="late"/>

has_value checks both shared commitments and private beliefs. The other has_*_value variants test their named store.

Child form for a service-action termination proposition:

<in_beliefs_or_commitments>
  <service_action_terminated name="BookRoom"/>
</in_beliefs_or_commitments>

Child form for a perform goal proposition:

<in_beliefs_or_commitments>
  <perform action="top"/>
</in_beliefs_or_commitments>

The service_action_terminated example checks only that the service call terminated, not whether it succeeded; see Invoke service action.

docs.title: Boolean composition
docs.text:
and and or take one or more nested conditions. not takes exactly one.

<and>
  <has_value predicate="destination"/>
  <not>
    <in_private_beliefs predicate="destination" value="paris"/>
  </not>
</and>

docs.title: DDD JSON
docs.text:
The JSON representation uses a single-key object per condition:

{
  "and": [
    {"has_value": {"predicate": "destination"}},
    {"not": {"in_private_beliefs": {"predicate": "destination", "value": "paris"}}}
  ]
}

The JSON schema and compiler also support or, in_* child propositions, has_more_items, and the other condition forms listed above.

has_more_items names either the predicate queried by a domain enumeration or the iterator:

<has_more_items predicate="possible_destination"/>
<has_more_items iterator="destination_iterator"/>

docs.title: Tala reference and tests
docs.text:
• XML condition grammar and child proposition forms: tala/ddd/schemas/domain.xsd
  • XML compilation: tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py
  • Truth evaluation: tala/model/condition.py
  • Tala tests: tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py and tala/model/test/test_condition.py

See also Downdate conditions and the archived condition examples.

docs.title: Downdate conditions
docs.text: A downdate_condition is a child of a goal. When the goal's condition becomes true, TDM treats the goal as fulfilled and downdates it. Multiple conditions on one goal are alternatives: any one true condition is sufficient.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <plan>
    <invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/>
  </plan>
  <downdate_condition>
    <in_beliefs_or_commitments>
      <service_action_terminated name="BookRoom"/>
    </in_beliefs_or_commitments>
  </downdate_condition>
</goal>

The child of downdate_condition is a normal condition expression. It can be a predicate/value condition, an in_* proposition condition, a value test, or a Boolean composition. Each condition is evaluated against the active TIS.

docs.title: Service actions: termination is not success
docs.text:
TDM records service_action_terminated whenever an invoked service action returns, including when its result is unsuccessful. With postconfirm, the termination proposition is stored in private beliefs; without it, it is stored in shared commitments. in_beliefs_or_commitments checks both locations. Therefore, this condition means “the service call ended,” not “the operation succeeded.”

The old invoke_service_action/@downdate_plan attribute does not create an implicit downdate condition in Tala/TDM 31.0.1. It is retained by the XML/JSON models for compatibility; author an explicit condition for current behavior.

docs.title: Downdate and cleanup behavior
docs.text:
TDM also downdates a perform/resolve goal when the corresponding action or question status is committed. For explicit conditions, TDM evaluates each condition and clears the propositions named by in_* conditions from the corresponding TIS store when the goal is downdated. Boolean and/or conditions clean their satisfied branches. has_value checks predicate presence without identifying a specific proposition to remove, and not does not remove facts.

The XML schema retains <postcond> as a compatibility form. New DDDs should use <downdate_condition>.

docs.title: Tala sources and examples
docs.text:
• Schema/compiler: tala/ddd/schemas/domain.xsd, tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py
  • Goal-to-condition mapping: tala/model/domain.py
  • Tala tests: tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py and tala/model/test/test_domain.py

See also Conditions and the archived downdate-condition article.

docs.title: Findout
docs.text: Tala 31.0.1 XML element: a question-raising plan item. A findout asks the user or invokes the configured question source to resolve its question. It differs from raise, which raises an issue without imposing the same findout plan behavior.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
<findout type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
Attribute Type Default Meaning type question type wh_question One of goal, wh_question, kpq, alt_question, or yn_question. predicate ontology predicate — Identifies a predicate-backed question when required by its type. allow_answer_from_pcom Boolean false Allows compatible answers from the user's previous commitments to be considered. alts_predicate ontology predicate — For a wh-question, supplies fact-backed alternatives from this predicate.

findout can be used in a goal plan, postplan, or a conditional plan. Its question form depends on type:

Type Question content goal Asks which goal/action is relevant; no predicate is needed. wh_question Uses the named predicate, e.g. predicate="destination". yn_question Uses a Boolean predicate or a proposition/goal child. alt_question Contains one or more alt children, each naming an alternative proposition or goal. kpq Contains an embedded_question describing the question whose answer is known.

docs.title: Parents and question children
docs.text:
findout may appear in a <plan>, <postplan>, or a <then>/<else> plan inside <if>. Its question content can be supplied by attributes or by child elements:

Child Use proposition Predicate proposition, commonly the content of a yes/no question. perform Perform-goal alternative, including a yes/no action question. resolve Resolve-goal alternative. alt Wraps an explicit alternative; repeat for each alternative. embedded_question The embedded question of a KPQ.

A KPQ embeds the question whose knowledge is being checked:

<findout type="kpq">
  <embedded_question type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
</findout>

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The DME raises the question represented by the plan item. When the DDD has question parameters, the configured domain/service query and question parameters may determine the answers or wording. allow_answer_from_pcom allows a compatible answer in the user's previous commitments to be reused; TDM applies its confidence and grounding rules before integrating that answer.

For a wh-question with alts_predicate, TDM collects positive known facts for that predicate. A single fact can be posed as a yes/no question; multiple facts can be posed as an alternative question. Define the ontology predicate with multiple_instances="true" when the domain needs to retain several values for it. A configured max_spoken_alts can limit the alternatives that are presented.

XML compatibility caveat: Tala 31.0.1's XSD declares allow_answer_from_pcom as Boolean, but the XML compiler tests attribute presence rather than its value. Omit the attribute to disable reuse and use allow_answer_from_pcom="true" to enable it; do not write allow_answer_from_pcom="false" in XML. DDD JSON uses a Boolean and does not have this presence-only behavior.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
WH and yes/no questions:

<findout type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
<findout type="yn_question" predicate="need_visa"/>
<findout type="goal"/>

Explicit alternatives, where each alternative is a question or goal proposition:

<findout type="alt_question">
  <alt><resolve type="wh_question" predicate="monthly_payment"/></alt>
  <alt><resolve type="wh_question" predicate="interest_rate"/></alt>
</findout>

An alternative may also be a perform goal:

<findout type="yn_question">
  <perform action="call_contact_from_history"/>
</findout>

KPQ in DDD JSON uses a nested question object:

{
  "findout": {
    "question": {
      "kpq": {"question": {"wh": {"predicate": "destination"}}}
    }
  }
}

Fact-backed alternatives and prior-commitment reuse:

<findout type="wh_question" predicate="animal"
         alts_predicate="available_animal"
         allow_answer_from_pcom="true"/>

DDD JSON equivalent for a basic wh-question:

{"findout": {"question": {"wh": {"predicate": "destination"}}}}

See domain XML, DDD JSON, and the archived Findout examples. The archived Alt child article has additional alternative-form examples.

docs.title: Tala reference and tests
docs.text:
• XML parsing/defaults: tala/ddd/ddd_xml_compiler.py
  • JSON compilation: tala/ddd/ddd_json_compiler.py
  • Plan item model: tala/model/plan_item.py
  • Tala tests: tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_xml_compiler.py and tala/ddd/test/test_ddd_json_compiler.py

docs.title: Invoke service action
docs.text: invoke_service_action requests an action declared by the current DDD's service interface. The action's name and parameter predicates must agree with that interface and the ontology.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
<invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"
                       preconfirm="interrogative"
                       postconfirm="true"/>
Attribute Type Default Meaning name string Required Service-interface action name. preconfirm assertive or interrogative None Selects the preconfirmation behavior before invocation. postconfirm Boolean false Requests a natural-language report about the result. downdate_plan Boolean, deprecated XML schema says true; Tala 31.0.1 compiler defaults a missing attribute to false Does not create implicit goal-downdate conditions in the current runtime.

Use lowercase XML Boolean values true and false. The downdate_plan schema/compiler default mismatch is retained here because it affects existing DDD interpretation; don't rely on that attribute for plan control.

docs.title: Execution and confirmation
docs.text:
The DME resolves the named action in the service interface, binds parameters, and issues the service call. preconfirm="interrogative" requires positive user preconfirmation before invocation. preconfirm="assertive" uses a system prereport as the confirmation step; the DME can proceed if the user does not object.

When postconfirm="true", TDM queues a report after the service result. It also queues a report when a call fails, even if postconfirmation is not requested. TDM records service_action_terminated whenever the call returns; that proposition does not indicate success. To end a goal based on service termination, write an explicit downdate condition.

docs.title: JSON form
docs.text:
{
  "invoke_service_action": {
    "name": "BookRoom",
    "preconfirm": "interrogative",
    "postconfirm": true
  }
}

The JSON model still permits downdate_plan for compatibility. New DDDs should use downdate_conditions on the goal.
